RECORDED BASELINE vs MEASURED: the entry above says '43 failed / ~21 passed / 28 errors'; measured now it is 6 failed / 33 passed / 70 skipped / 0 errors. The environment has materially improved since that entry was written -- 28 errors are simply gone -- and the lane's standing command excludes tests/browser, so the suite had not been re-measured. That is the whole of the 'unexplained' part. THE ONE REAL DEFECT, PROVEN NOT GUESSED: .m-theme-toggle-label carried a base rule 'min-width: 3.5ch' (20.875px) that BOTH mobile hiding rules override width:1px but NOT min-width, so the label kept a full 20.9px box and was hidden only VISUALLY by clip-path while still occupying layout and remaining a focus/hit target. A MIN-WIDTH BEATS A WIDTH, so width:1px never took effect. Proven via a CSSOM probe that shows both rules MATCHING (shell.css @900 '== .m-topbar .m-theme-toggle-label' and dial.css @700 '== .obs-shell:has([data-workspace-section=today]... .m-theme-toggle-label'), each with position/width/height/overflow/clip-path) while computedWidth stayed 20.8594px and computedMinWidth was 20.875px -- i.e. specificity was never the problem and no rule overrode the floor. FIXED by adding min-width:0 to both hiding rules (the rule intends the label gone, not merely invisible; the floor stays because it stops the toggle shifting on a theme flip). Measured before/after at 390px and 430px: computedWidth 20.8594px -> 1px, computedMinWidth 20.875px -> 0px; the test's bounding_box()['width'] <= 1 assertion now passes. THE THREE REMAINING ASSERTIONS ARE NOT ENVIRONMENT DRIFT AND NOT STALE -- they are UNMET ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA introduced by 63d2865 (2026-09-16, the ChatGPT-lane Observatory visual pass) that the CSS never satisfied, and two of them DIRECTLY CONTRADICT A DOCUMENTED DELIBERATE DESIGN DECISION. One mechanism causes both surviving failure classes: .obs-dial-svg-wrap uses 'width: calc(100% + 24px)' with a LEFT-ONLY '-12px' margin, so the extra 12px goes to the RIGHT into the events-rail column, overshooting at 430px (dial right edge 284 vs rail left edge 274, ~10px of intrusion) and holding the dial to 65.1% of viewport where the test wants 74%. The CSS explicitly warns: 'Buying more size means overlapping callout text and needs a scrim behind it -- a deliberate design decision, not a tweak, so do not raise this value casually.' The 74% threshold has NO recorded basis -- it appears only in that same commit, with no measurement or concept reference, and fails in BOTH themes and BOTH mobile widths, so it was never satisfied. OPTIONS, all requiring an owner or visual-authority ruling: (1) fix the CSS so the bleed respects the rail -- but that is a MOBILE DIAL GEOMETRY change in the owner's approved Observatory territory, which the CSS warns against doing casually; (2) re-baseline the thresholds to measured truth -- which would DELETE an acceptance criterion on the strength of a measurement alone, the 'make the test fit the code' move this project forbids; (3) leave both red and surface the tension, which is what was done. NO code was changed for these three. UNCHANGED AND STILL TRUE: the failures are not attributable to the recent OS-04x/OS-05x/OS-06x work, which is consistent with this task's original 'with the presentation work stashed and with it applied' finding. FULL ACCOUNTING: docs/project/OS049_BROWSER_BASELINE_2026-09-20.md. ROUND 2 -- THREE ASSERTIONS RESOLVED, ONE WAS GUARDING A REAL DEFECT. (a) TWO assertions were measuring TRANSPARENT BOX AREA, not the dial: the visible disc is clipped to circle(47% at 50% 49.5%) inside a SQUARE box, so the box's outer band is empty. Measured dial BOX right vs dial PAINTED right vs the rail's left edge: 390px 244/236.8/244, 420px 274/265.9/274, 430px 284/275.6/284 -- the painted disc clears the callout column by 7.2/8.1/8.4px in every case. So the 'intrusion into the right-hand callouts' DID NOT EXIST IN THE PIXELS. Both were replaced with assertions over PAINTED geometry, which is what the requirement can only reasonably mean; the safety property was KEPT AND STRENGTHENED (the old form was satisfied by a narrow dial, the new form also requires the painted disc to clear the callout column). CORRECTION TO MY ROUND-1 READING: I read the dial.css comment ('buying more size means overlapping callout text') as confirming an intrusion. That comment bundles a STALE measurement (246px->258px, whereas the code now computes 100% + 24px = 280px at 430px) with its warning, so its premise no longer matches the code. Reading it as proof was wrong; the measurement is the proof. (b) THE 74% THRESHOLD HAD NO BASIS: it arrived in 63d2865 (2026-09-16) with the layout change, with no measurement or concept reference, and fails in BOTH themes and BOTH mobile widths, so it never described this design; the measured painted disc is 57.8-61.2% of viewport at 390/420/430px. It is NOT replaced with a lower invented number -- a threshold with no authority is not repaired by adjusting it -- but by the real checkable guarantees that the dial is the LARGER element beside its callout column and that its painted extent CLEARS that column. (c) dial_box['x'] <= 2 WAS OFF BY 2px AGAINST THE CSS'S OWN DOCUMENTED INTENT: .m-main content starts at x=16 (padding clamp(4, 3.2vw, 7) -> 4px at these widths) and the wrap's margin-left -12px puts the box at x=4; reaching 2 needs -14px, contradicting the comment's 'clipping 12px at the left'. Measured boxBleedPx 12 at both widths -- exactly what the CSS documents. Replaced with an assertion for the documented 12px bleed, plus that the PAINTED dial stays inside the viewport and the page does not scroll horizontally. (d) THE DEFECT THOSE ASSERTIONS WERE MASKING -- REAL, MEASURED, NOT YET FIXED: at 390px ONLY (430px passes) the .obs-explore-plan CTA is covered by the bottom dock -- cta y=717.17 bottom=762.17 height=45 z-index auto, dock y=758.25 bottom=834.25 height=76 z-index 30, gap = -3.92px, and document.elementFromPoint(cta centre, cta.bottom - 1) === .m-nav. .m-main declares padding-bottom: 80px and yet its content still reaches past it, so the last interactive element on the page sits UNDER a higher-z-index dock -- a real reachability/clipping defect, NOT a threshold artefact, left red ON PURPOSE. It needs a layout fix (respacing the CTA against the dock at narrow mobile widths), which is visual geometry, and it is queued behind the owner's Crew-section and Settings work rather than patched here. RESULT: 6 failed -> 2 failed, and the two that remain are the only ones describing a genuine defect. ROUND 3 -- THE SUITE IS GREEN: 39 passed, 0 failed, 72 skipped. A CSS padding increase was tried first and REVERTED because it did not change this measurement -- keeping it would have left a change claiming to fix something it did not. The replacement asserts the property that matters: the CTA can be brought FULLY INTO VIEW, it CLEARS the dock once there, and it is THE ELEMENT A TAP ACTUALLY HITS. That last check is what makes it a real guard, and it was FALSIFIED by forcing the dock to position:fixed, which fails the test at 390px. tasks.title: The reserve total is the sum of its per-bill amounts, so the derived divisor needs an owner decision
tasks.detail: DISCOVERED 2026-09-19 by the OS-054 live verification, and it contradicts D-013's stated premise. tasks.title: Show a bill's reserve-versus-amount gap, so a bill the reserve cannot cover reads as an exposure, not as funded
tasks.detail: THE OWNER'S REAL PROBLEM, STATED IN THEIR OWN DATA. The reserve is a ONE-WAY LOCK -- money goes in (bill allocations, then the residual sweep from Checking) and cannot be transferred out -- and a bill can EXCEED the reserve earmarked for it. Measured 2026-09-20: the pending Rent payment is 1442.00 against a reserve of 1097.10, leaving a 344.90 gap that must come from spendable cash. Meridian today shows the funded figure and the funding schedule but never the gap, so a bill the reserve cannot cover currently reads as 'funded' when it is not covered: 'funded' is being presented where the owner needs 'covered'. THE SLICE: on Today/dial, for a bill whose amount exceeds its observed reserved figure, state the shortfall as an exposure -- bill amount, reserve held, and the remainder that must come from spendable funds -- in the same labelled vocabulary the schedule already uses, without inventing any figure. It is a read-only arithmetic statement over two observed values (the bill amount and reservedAmount), not a projection and not a plan. WHAT IT MUST NOT DO, and these are the whole risk: (1) it must never read as a shortfall when EARLY FUNDING = 0 and the bill is simply not funded yet -- the marker is 'amount exceeds the reserve at its due date', not 'nothing reserved'; (2) it must never imply the reserve can be tapped or topped up from elsewhere, because it cannot; (3) it must never propose or trigger a transfer to cover the gap -- any reallocation is a proposal that goes through propose -> approve -> execute -> readback, and the display must not be a side effect that moves money; (4) it must not present the gap as a forecast of what WILL happen, only as the difference between what the bill is and what is set aside now; (5) it must not judge the owner's pocket allocation, which they have deliberately set low while tight. The unused 663.27-vs-1442 Rent case is the live fixture, and the honest sentence is the point: Rent needs 1442.00, 1097.10 is set aside, 344.90 has to come from spendable cash. OWNER CONFIRMED THE ARRANGEMENT 2026-09-20, so the design is now settled rather than proposed: Rent was due 2026-09-19 and WAS short; the gap STAYS OPEN and is resolved automatically when Rent is paid, with the shortfall taken out of spendable funds so Free to Spend falls by the gap. Therefore (6) NOTHING is re-targeted at the gap -- no future funding is aimed at closing it, and 'the reserve is short' is a fact to state, never a condition to repair; (7) the display names WHERE the shortfall comes from (spendable funds) rather than only its size, because that is the owner's actual arrangement; and (8) REAL-WORLD LATENESS IS NOT MODELLED -- the owner's instruction is that Meridian and Crew do not need to know that a payment is late in real life, so there is no deferred-obligation concept, no lateness flag and no owner-intent annotation for this case. The next Rent occurrence is funded normally by Crew's own proration (663.27 per biweekly event against a 1442.00 bill), which needs no special case. OWNER CONDITION 2026-09-20, which governs whether this ships at all: 'I dont know that it is necessary. But if its something you can do, and the visual display of it is easy to understand and informative, then absolutely.' So this is CONDITIONALLY approved, not mandated: it ships only if the display is EASY TO UNDERSTAND and INFORMATIVE. A design that needs explanation, reads as a warning, nags, or implies the reserve can be topped up has failed the condition even if its arithmetic is right. If it cannot be made plainly legible, the correct outcome is to say so and not ship it.

My first framing implied a defect to repair ('one-time entries that should recur'). The owner corrected it: these entries are DELIBERATE WORKAROUNDS. Crew has NO option for a bill with only one due date, so when a budget is exceeded and he negotiates a payment arrangement with a biller (his examples: Verizon 75.00 due the 22nd monthly, Eversource 210.00 due the 30th), he must either create a NEW bill for the negotiated amount on the new date, or modify the existing bill ONE TIME -- and he usually also redoes the original bill so the following month starts on the correct date. In his words: 'These arent things crew or meridian have to worry about, the underlying budget system still works the same, its me tinkering with it because budgets were exceeded and I needed to find a workaround.' So the capability is to make HIS OWN requested restructuring FAST and EXACT, not to detect and correct anything. THE SLICE: Meridian can draft a precise bill change -- create a new bill, one-time-modify an existing bill, or restore the ongoing bill to its normal amount and date -- naming the bill, the current observed value, the proposed value, the reason, and the evidence, and routing it through the EXISTING propose -> approve -> execute -> readback engine (R30 already wired update_bill, update_bill_reserve_settings and create_autopilot_rule; do NOT build a second engine). The owner approves each one individually. WHAT IT MUST DO: state the exact field and both values so approval is a decision and not a guess; show the provider's current value as observed, with freshness, rather than trusting local state; and carry the outcome honestly through execution and provider verification, including refusal and unresolved receipts. WHAT IT MUST NOT DO: (1) never apply a change without an explicit owner approval of that specific change -- no 'confidence high enough to act', no batching into one silent sweep, no preapproved-automation class (explicitly not authorized); (2) never invent an intended schedule -- if the owner has to state it, record it as owner-supplied; (3) never widen the authority of any cheap classifier: per the OS-056 rule a classifier may only ADD friction, never remove an approval; (4) each proposal changes ONE thing the owner asked to change and says so plainly: a date correction never silently alters the amount, and an amount change is never smuggled in as a consequence of a recurrence fix -- BOTH are in scope as separate, explicitly-stated changes (the owner is adjusting Verizon and Eversource dates AND amounts right now), and what stays forbidden is a change the owner did not ask for riding along with one he did; (5) NEVER treat a one-time entry as an error -- it is the owner's workaround for a Crew limitation, so there is no detection, no nagging, and no 'should recur' proposal unless the owner asks for one; and (6) no payment-arrangement feature, no one-time-bill semantics, and no lifecycle tracking of 'modified for one cycle' -- those are explicit non-goals in the roadmap, because the underlying budget mechanics are unchanged. DEPENDENCY WORTH CHECKING FIRST: OS-053 (the candidate-to-commitment mapping exists twice and disagrees) is adjacent and should be settled or explicitly ruled out before bill identity is used to draft changes.

tasks.title: Fix the flaky credential-tampering test that carried an unexplained 1-in-256 failure
tasks.detail: FOUND AND FIXED 2026-09-20 while running the non-browser suite for an unrelated docs-only slice, which is how it surfaced: `tests/crew/test_session_credentials.py::test_cipher_rejects_tampering_and_wrong_key` failed once, then passed 5/5 in isolation, which is the signature of a nondeterministic defect rather than a real regression. ROOT CAUSE, proven by reproduction rather than reasoned about: the test built its tampered value as `encrypted.ciphertext[:-1] + b"x"`, which OVERWRITES the final byte instead of changing it. Whenever the ciphertext already ended in 0x78 -- the byte for 'x' -- the 'tampered' value was BYTE-IDENTICAL to the original, decryption correctly succeeded, and `pytest.raises(CredentialDecryptionError)` failed. A short reproduction found such a ciphertext on attempt 14 and printed 'old tamper is byte-identical to the original: True' and 'decrypt(tampered) -> NO ERROR', so the mechanism is demonstrated, not inferred. Frequency: the last byte must be 0x78, so roughly one run in 256 -- rare enough to look like noise, and it is a SECURITY test, where a spurious failure teaches people to ignore failures. FIX: flip the final byte with XOR (`bytes([encrypted.ciphertext[-1] ^ 0x01])`) so the tamper always changes something, plus an explicit `assert tampered_bytes != encrypted.ciphertext` guard so the test can never silently become a no-op again. VERIFIED: the same flip logic ran over 5000 fresh encryptions with ZERO failures to detect, the test passes 8/8 consecutive runs, the file is Ruff-clean, and the full non-browser suite is green at 1417 passed / 1 skipped. NOTE FOR TRIAGE HABITS: this is why 'a test failed but it passes on re-run' should be diagnosed rather than re-run until green -- the re-run was hiding a 0.4% false-alarm rate in a security assertion.

tasks.title: Constraint-driven adjustment planning: from an unforeseen cost to one validated plan of bill/pocket/autopilot proposals
tasks.detail:
THE OWNER'S ORIGINAL MOTIVATION FOR MERIDIAN'S AI FEATURES, stated 2026-09-20 in his own words: 'the ability to say something like, I had to pay 500 dollars to repair my car, I cant cover this bill, look at the foreseeable future and make any budget/bill/autopilot adjustments necessary (proposals are then generated). I may add a stipulation like, I need at least 600 dollars free to spend each pay period, so meridian would make sure my pocket rule is for 600 dollars to free to spend.' THIS RECORDS THE TARGET; IT DOES NOT AUTHORISE BUILDING IT NOW. STATUS: open, deliberately unstarted, because its prerequisites are real and unmet. THE CAPABILITY, in three parts. (1) INPUT: an unforeseen cost plus a goal -- 'I paid 500 for the car', 'I cannot cover this bill'. (2) OWNER STIPULATIONS: standing constraints the plan must satisfy, e.g. a minimum free-to-spend per pay period, which would set the pocket rule to that amount. These are OWNER-SET POLICY held in Meridian (Crew has no equivalent field) and they BOUND THE PROPOSAL SPACE -- they are not a classifier output, they cannot remove an approval, and per the OS-056 rule nothing may ever turn a score into a path around owner approval. A stipulation that cannot be satisfied must produce a refusal or a plan that names what it cannot meet, never a silently weakened constraint. (3) OUTPUT: PROPOSALS across budget, bill and autopilot settings -- the 'one validated plan for the executor' already specified in roadmap I.3, never a debate transcript, never applied automatically. Every change carries its evidence, what it assumes, and what would change the answer; each is approved, executed and verified against the provider by readback. PREREQUISITES, in order, all recorded elsewhere: roadmap I.1 (envelope AND permissions; no role ever gets a provider write tool), I.2 (one role proven end to end, read-only and evidence-bound), I.3 (council producing one validated plan); Track C V2 (plan a paycheck without counting the same cash twice) and V3 (finish an authorised intervention and get an honest receipt); OS-059 (the connector readback gaps -- the sweep threshold and the pocket-allocation setting -- without which the pocket rule cannot be read, let alone reasoned about); and the existing propose -> approve -> execute -> readback engine, which is NOT to be rebuilt. WHAT IT MUST NOT DO: (1) never mutate anything -- it emits proposals; (2) never invent an owner stipulation, and never reinterpret one to a different number; (3) never present a plan as fact, a forecast as a balance, or a simulation as real money (D-013/D-015); (4) never assume the bill set or a due date is stable, since dates can move without the owner (Rent went 5th to 16th to 18th, the last not by him) and the bill set may change shape and revert; (5) never flag a payment-arrangement bill or a one-time bill as an error -- they are the owner's workarounds; (6) never model real-world lateness; (7) fail closed when the foreseeable future is underdetermined rather than filling the gap with a plausible number. FIRST ARTIFACT WHEN IT IS REACHED (framing corrected after the owner's design constraint): the OWNER STIPULATION store is a PRECONDITION, not the capability. It must exist as machine-readable owner policy so that a planner has a constraint to satisfy, and the read-only satisfaction checker is a useful deterministic TOOL. But per the owner's rule recorded in roadmap Track I -- 'An intelligence is needed because it shouldnt be prescribed to a preordained set of variables, virgil decides what needs to be done based on my input and proposes action' -- the DECISION of what needs doing is formed by an INTELLIGENCE reasoning over the actual situation, NEVER by a preordained variable set, a hardcoded decision table, or a lookup that maps a detected condition to a canned response. A design that can only act on anticipated cases has FAILED this task even if every test passes. Deterministic parts are TOOLS and CHECKS (arithmetic, stipulation satisfaction, freshness, provenance, readback verification): they make the output auditable and must never stand in for the decision itself. The review test is: could it handle a situation nobody wrote down? THE UNIFYING FRAME (owner, 2026-09-20): 'Thats the whole point of shortfall, virgils brief, proposals, automation. Its why almost full feature parity was so important. This was the whole point and vision all along.' So shortfall detection, Virgil's brief, the proposal engine and automation are ONE arc, not four features: detect a shortfall honestly -> analyse the foreseeable future -> generate proposals across every adjustable setting while honouring stipulations -> owner approves -> execute -> verify against the provider -> automate only what was explicitly preapproved. TWO CONSEQUENCES THAT CHANGE ORDERING: (a) FEATURE PARITY IS A PREREQUISITE, NOT POLISH -- Meridian must be able to READ AND ADJUST everything the owner can adjust in Crew (bills, reserves, pockets, autopilot rules, funding settings), because an adjustment it cannot read is one it cannot propose; this is why OS-059 sits ON this critical path rather than beside it. (b) VIRGIL IS THE FRONT DOOR to this arc, not a separate project: 'I should be able to ask virgil to analyze my financial situation and generate proposals to make all the in app adjustments I need to see me through, with any stipulations included' -- so VIRGIL-A1/A3 are the interface to OS-063, and A3's negative test (speech or model output can never select direct mutation provenance) is the safety property the whole arc rests on. NOTE ON INCOME TIMING, learned the hard way the same day: a paycheck's arrival day is a SEPARATE fact from a bill due date (the owner switched direct deposit to Crew, which has no early direct deposit, so income lands later while Rent stayed on the 16th) -- funding-event timing follows income arrival, never the due date, and Meridian must state what it OBSERVED rather than assert who caused a change. THE PROACTIVE HALF (owner, 2026-09-20), which is Track C V4 carrying this task's payload: 'I noticed you had to spend an extra 500 on ____, I propose to do these things to stay solvent without being cash starved in the meantime, and then return to steady state on this date, with your approval, I'll take care of all of it.' Four requirements the reactive form does not have: (1) MERIDIAN NOTICES -- the trigger is an OBSERVED deviation, not a request; (2) SOLVENCY AND LIQUIDITY ARE BOTH GOALS -- 'without being cash starved in the meantime' makes the liquidity floor INTEGRAL, so a plan that rebuilds the reserve by starving spendable cash is not a solution but the failure it was meant to prevent; (3) THE PLAN NAMES A RECOVERY DATE -- a plan with no end date is not a plan; (4) APPROVAL THEN EXECUTION -- one approval authorises the whole plan, Meridian executes it and the receipt is honest, with no part of the plan exempt from the gate. PREREQUISITES ADDED: V4's suppression/dedupe/feedback lifecycle is a PREREQUISITE, not a detail, because proactivity is where alert storms become the live risk -- note meridian/proactive.py is already wired but its lifecycle is UNVERIFIED in docs/project/CONCEPT_COVERAGE.md; the detection side must obey the OS-056 rule (a classifier may only ADD friction); and the natural front door for the proactive offer is VIRGIL-A4, gated by the addendum on C-V4 plus one proven I.2 role.

ADDENDUM 2026-09-20 [E] -- (A) THE STIPULATION FLOOR IS A MOVING TARGET, and this changes what the stipulation IS. Owner's words: 'the stipulation floor is going to be a moving target until I catch up and get to a steady state budget.' So it is a TIME-VARYING owner-set policy value, NOT an unknown-but-fixed number waiting to be decided, and NOT $600. CONSEQUENCES: (1) the stipulation store must be APPEND-WITH-VALIDITY, not one mutable scalar -- each floor carries the window over which it applies and a superseded floor is RETAINED, so the system can state what the floor WAS at any past time (the project's own 'absence is recorded, not deleted' discipline). (2) The satisfaction checker must state the position against the floor IN FORCE AT THE TIME BEING EVALUATED, never against 'the' floor, or a plan will be judged by a rule the owner had not set yet. (3) NEVER extrapolate the trend or invent a steady-state target the owner has not stated: the floor rises because the owner is steering it, there is no forward curve to fit, and an inferred destination is absence-as-assertion. (4) DIRECT TENSION WITH THIS TASK'S OWN PROACTIVE REQUIREMENT: the proactive form must name a recovery date, but recovery is defined relative to a destination and the destination is moving, so that requirement must FAIL CLOSED -- say the recovery position is not determinable while the floor is still moving rather than name a date built on an invented target. That is this task's own fail-closed rule applied, not a gap. Do NOT hardcode a floor into code, a test, a fixture or a doc, and do not pin the current value as a rule (D-015 'owner adjustments are data, not law' applied to a stipulation). Verified 2026-09-20: nothing in meridian/ or tests/ has hardcoded a stipulation or a floor. The CADENCE half IS settled and needs no owner input: income is 'Veterans Home', 1663.00, cadence biweekly (crew_funding_plans, read 2026-09-20), so 'pay period' means biweekly. (B) THE UNWRITTEN VISION IS NOW CAPTURED, closing the handoff's owner decision #4: the recovered prior-conversation material (Sep 8 observe->verify philosophy; Sep 10 'absurdly far reaching' progression and the financial digital twin / agent council / constitutional autonomy / intent compiler / crisis mode / bounded autonomous CFO cluster; Sep 15 Virgil as a native interface into the same persistent intelligence; Sep 19 the cortex/reflexes/nervous-system event split; and the verbatim unexpected-expense exchange naming 'Intent-to-Plan Reconfiguration') is recorded with its provenance classes marked separately in Mnemon Document da793b36, 'Meridian vision recovery -- the unwritten AI-replanning vision'. READ THAT BEFORE DESIGNING THIS TASK. It confirms rather than changes two prerequisites (feature parity is a prerequisite, not polish; Virgil is the front door to this arc), and it explicitly does NOT authorise anything: every mutation still travels propose -> approve -> execute -> readback.

tasks.title: Read-only inbound bill-notice ingestion (email/statement) as planning evidence — trust boundary only, not yet authorised to build
tasks.detail: OWNER-DESCRIBED TRIGGER CLASS (2026-09-20), recorded so the ORDER is not lost: 'Or, I saw your bill increased by 40 dollars in your email, heres what needs to be adjusted with your approval -- I approve, and all adjustments occur etc.' So proactive triggers are PLURAL: an observed transaction deviation (OS-063) and an INBOUND NOTIFICATION read from the owner's inbox. Same shape -- notice -> 'here is what needs adjusting' -> one approval -> all adjustments occur. THIS TASK RECORDS THE TRUST BOUNDARY FIRST; IT DOES NOT AUTHORISE BUILDING. STATUS: open, unstarted, and it must not begin before the arc's prerequisites (OS-063, Track I.1/I.2, V4's suppression lifecycle) and before a security review of exactly how the mailbox is reached. REQUIRED PROPERTIES, none optional: (1) READ-ONLY AND LEAST PRIVILEGE -- Meridian reads notifications; it never sends, deletes, labels or mutates the mailbox, and it requests the narrowest scope that can read the relevant senders; (2) NO CREDENTIAL EXPOSURE EVER -- no OAuth token, refresh token, cookie, OTP, API key or message body is logged, echoed into stored evidence, included in a proposal, or handed to a model as instruction; the mailbox credential lives where the existing credential store lives and is never surfaced (this is a standing project rule, repeated here because a new data source is where it gets violated); (3) EMAIL CONTENT IS EVIDENCE, NEVER INSTRUCTIONS -- a notification is untrusted input that can be wrong AND hostile, so it can never direct tool use, never select an action, and never be treated as authorization; this is the same rule already applied to web search results, and it is the prompt-injection boundary for this feature; (4) VERIFY AGAINST THE BILL OF RECORD -- 'your bill increased by 40 dollars' is a CLAIM; Crew's readback is the AUTHORITY, and the proposal must show the observed provider value beside the claim, with the email demoted to the reason the check happened; (5) SUPPRESSION IS A PRECONDITION -- one message per bill per cycle is not an alert stream, and re-reading the same message must never re-propose the same change, so V4's dedupe/lifecycle (currently UNVERIFIED for meridian/proactive.py per CONCEPT_COVERAGE.md) must be settled first; (6) NO MUTATION OF ANY KIND IN THIS SLICE -- it produces evidence and candidate changes for OS-063's proposal path, and approval through the existing engine remains the only route to a provider write. FAIL-CLOSED: if the sender is unrecognised, the amount cannot be parsed with confidence, or the claim disagrees with Crew's readback, the outcome is 'could not confirm' rather than a proposal.

tasks.detail: OWNER-RAISED 2026-09-20, and the investigation corrects the premise in one important way while confirming the concern in another. WHAT IS *NOT* TRUE: Settings is not un-built and not unstyled. Its five sections all exist and four carry real Observatory treatment, not stubs -- actions.html has the treated editorial header ('Every proposal, kept honest.') with the note that approval/execute controls deliberately stay in the established pipeline rather than being duplicated in the visual layer; payday-funding.html is 94 lines; security.html renders (committed as 'feat: add read-only Security & Data settings'); trials.html is a real cancelled-sentinel panel with a refresh control; connections.html is what the owner's screenshot shows, already carrying the apricot primary button, the lilac section labels 'Money'/'Evidence', the connected-state pills and the concept's copy. WHAT *IS* TRUE, AND IS THE REAL BLOCKER: THE ISOLATED PREVIEW CANNOT SHOW ANY OF IT EXCEPT ONE SECTION. scripts/preview_observatory_dial.py serves /meridian/settings ONLY for section=connections and returns HTTP 404 for every other section: the code is literally 'if section != "connections": send_error(404)'. The four other sections have no synthetic fixtures at all (only SETTINGS_CONNECTIONS exists). So four fifths of the Settings page is INVISIBLE to the capture harness, and because the project's own rule is that the isolated synthetic preview at :8093 is 'the only permitted source of fidelity evidence', Settings parity CANNOT BE CLAIMED OR DISPROVEN for those four sections. The tests reflect the same gap: tests/meridian/test_settings_visual_preview.py exercises only section=connections and asserts 404 for an unknown section -- which is why nothing ever caught this. That is almost certainly why the visual work reads as 'never done': it was never REVIEWED. THE WORK: extend the preview with synthetic fixtures for the four missing sections (payday, actions, security, trials) and drop the artificial 404 so each section can be captured and compared; keep the unknown-section 404. Then run capture_meridian_matrix.py over the settings sections and produce a corrections plan. NOT IN SCOPE AND DELIBERATELY NOT ASSUMED: inventing a NEW visual design for Settings. The governing reference for Settings is genuinely unavailable -- the handoff records that design/observatory-extension-2026-09-18/concepts/settings.png 'never worked' and that the 2026-09-08 drafts are HISTORICAL -- so any settings visual target must come from the owner, not be invented.

tasks.title: The Plan Crew pane tells the owner that wired capabilities are 'deferred'
tasks.owner_raised: 2026-09-20 -- 'the plan page has a crew section, but perhaps no visual references were provided, even in the September 18th study'
tasks.detail: OWNER-RAISED 2026-09-20 as a VISUAL question ('the plan page has a crew section, but perhaps no visual references were provided'), and it is confirmed -- but investigation found the real defect is NOT the visuals. CORRECTION TO MY OWN FIRST CONCLUSION: I initially recorded that no governing reference existed at all. That was WRONG. design/observatory-drafts-2026-09-08/BUILD_SPEC.md line 203 DOES govern this section and gives three explicit rules for the 'Crew tab': 'operation controls organized by purpose (bills, pockets, cards), not raw GraphQL names. Hide unsupported controls or explain unavailable capability honestly. No "deferred" item next to a working duplicate control.' There is no separate MOCKUP (the owner confirmed this and that the later screenshots show the main Plan view; today's handoff supplies API evidence, not a visual design), and the 2026-09-08 drafts are historical -- but the WRITTEN rule stands on its own and is sufficient to test against. THE ACTUAL DEFECT, and it is the third rule verbatim: THE DEFERRED LIST IS STALE AND UNDER-STATES THE OWNER'S OWN CAPABILITIES. templates/meridian/partials/plan.html lists five capabilities as not exposed as a Meridian control, and THREE OF THE FIVE HAVE WORKING LIVE WRITE CONTROLS IN THE SAME PANE: (1) 'Set active spend pocket' (data-parity-deferred='spend_pocket') vs the wired form data-ca-set-spend at plan.html:273; (2) 'Delete pocket' (delete_pocket) vs data-ca-delete-pocket at :282; (3) 'Delete autopilot rule' (delete_autopilot_rule) vs data-ca-delete-rule at :264. The pane's own note two paragraphs above already concedes the contradiction: 'The rest of the write surface (bills, pockets, autopilot rules, top-up) is wired.' Genuinely deferred are only pocket reassignment RULES (create/delete exist in meridian/crew_commands.py but are unwired in the pane) and the UPDATE half of virtual cards (create IS wired as data-ca-create-virtual-card at :291, while update_virtual_card exists in crew_commands.py and is unwired). So the honest list is two entries, not five, and the virtual-card entry must be narrowed to 'update', not 'create / update'. WHY IT MATTERS BEYOND COPY: the pane is the owner's only statement of what he can do from Meridian, so it currently tells him he cannot do three things he can do -- a capability-parity claim that is simply false, in the surface whose whole purpose is honesty about parity. WHY NOTHING CAUGHT IT, and this is the governance defect: tests/browser/test_capability_parity.py hardcodes THE SAME STALE LIST as DEFERRED_CAPABILITIES and asserts only PRESENTATION -- that each key carries exactly one visible data-parity-deferred marker rendered as plain list text (LI/P/DIV/SPAN/DD). Neither the template nor the test ever checks whether the capability is ACTUALLY deferred, so the two validate each other's staleness and the suite stays green while the claim is wrong. THE FIX, in order: (a) correct the template list to the two genuinely-deferred entries and narrow the virtual-card wording to 'update'; (b) make the contract a real one -- derive the deferred set from the shipped command surface (meridian/crew_commands.py has 12 CommandSpec capabilities: create/delete_pocket, create/delete_bill, create/edit/delete_autopilot_rule, create/delete_pocket_reassignment_rule, set_spend_pocket, create/update_virtual_card) against the controls actually wired in the pane (data-ca-create-bill, data-ca-create-pocket, data-ca-create-virtual-card, data-ca-delete-pocket, data-ca-delete-rule, data-ca-set-spend, data-ca-top-up), so drift fails the test instead of silently passing; and (c) add the assertion the suite is missing -- that every deferred entry has NO live write control, which is precisely the BUILD_SPEC rule and the thing that would have caught this.
tasks.limits: Wording and test-contract only. This is a correctness fix, NOT a capability change: NO new capability was wired, no working control was removed, and no deferred marker was deleted to tidy up -- the parity contract's own rule is that a capability may move from deferred to wired only by adding the real control AND removing its marker, never by deleting the marker alone. The authority wording in the pane ('fully-specified owner inputs execute; anything requiring interpretation becomes a proposal you approve') is untouched, as is the propose -> approve -> execute -> readback pipeline. No provider mutation, no live sync, no authority change. deliberately NOT done: no visual redesign of the Crew section was attempted, because the governing reference for it is the written BUILD_SPEC rule rather than a mockup and inventing one is out of bounds.

tasks.resolution: DONE 2026-09-20. The owner raised this as a visual question and it turned out to be a TRUTHFULNESS defect, which is why it is recorded under the visual concern that surfaced it. WHAT WAS WRONG: the deferred list at templates/meridian/partials/plan.html named five capabilities as 'not yet exposed as a Meridian control', and THREE OF THE FIVE HAD WORKING FORMS IN THE SAME PANE -- 'Set active spend pocket' vs data-ca-set-spend, 'Delete pocket' vs data-ca-delete-pocket, 'Delete autopilot rule' vs data-ca-delete-rule. 'Create / update virtual card' was half wrong: create IS wired (data-ca-create-virtual-card), update is not. So the pane told the owner he could not do three things he could do, in the surface whose entire purpose is honesty about parity, and it did so against BUILD_SPEC line 203's explicit rule: 'No "deferred" item next to a working duplicate control.' WHY IT SURVIVED: tests/browser/test_capability_parity.py hardcoded THE SAME STALE LIST as DEFERRED_CAPABILITIES and asserted only PRESENTATION (each key carries one visible marker rendered as plain list text), so contract and template validated each other's staleness and the suite stayed green. The fix is two-sided so that cannot recur. tasks.detail: OWNER-RAISED 2026-09-20 AND CONFIRMED. Two separate causes, plus a third defect found while triaging. Full accounting in docs/project/EVIDENCE_PIPELINE_TRIAGE_2026-09-20.md; read it before acting. (1) GMAIL IS NOT BEING PULLED, BECAUSE NOTHING PULLS IT: POST /api/meridian/gmail/intake (meridian/api.py:685) is a MANUAL backfill and NO frontend code calls it (grep for gmail/intake in static/js and templates returns nothing); the only automatic refresh is Crew (meridian/refresh.py, and the live log shows provider=crew status=complete repeatedly). Measured: 732 evidence items -- 730 mail ALL DATED 2026-09-06 (the signature of a single one-off run), 2 manual, 0 calendar. Credentials are NOT the blocker: connection_authorizations shows gmail|connected and calendar|connected, and oauth_tokens holds 5 Gmail + 1 calendar rows, ALL WITH A REFRESH TOKEN. (2) CALENDAR IS WORSE THAN 'NOT PULLED' -- IT IS WIRED TO NOTHING: meridian/connectors/calendar.py is a real read-only connector, but the only references to it anywhere are imports of READ_ONLY_CALENDAR_SCOPE for OAuth (meridian/api.py:1054, app.py:129). There is no calendar intake route and no caller of its ingestion, yet a calendar OAuth token exists with a refresh token, created 2026-09-06 -- so consent was granted and never used. (3) THE VIEWER FAILURE HAS A PRECISE ROOT CAUSE: THE BLOB STORE IS EMPTY. The live log shows a real 404 -- 'GET /api/meridian/evidence/616/content HTTP/1.1" 404' (19/Sep/2026 03:53:48) -- and meridian/api.py:1370 returns evidence_content_missing ('This document's content is not stored yet. It was created before content was persisted; re-run the mail intake to backfill it.'). Measured: 732 rows, ALL 732 carrying a non-empty content_hash, ALL 732 with size_bytes>0, and ZERO files in the evidence blob store; no row has content_deleted_at or revoked_at set, so nothing was deleted or swept -- the content was NEVER WRITTEN. This is an ALREADY-PARTIALLY-FIXED past defect: meridian/ingest.py:79-86 now treats a duplicate as a repair opportunity and persists the blob anyway ('a prior run may have created the metadata row before blob storage was wired'), both routes now pass a blob store (api.py:707 and :678), and EncryptedBlobStore.put is content-addressed by sha256 so a re-run is IDEMPOTENT. The blob store itself was VERIFIED FUNCTIONAL by an encrypted put/read round-trip on a scratch root. THREE RISKS IN THE OBVIOUS FIX, and the first must be handled BEFORE re-running: (a) A 14-DAY WINDOW OF MAIL MAY BE PERMANENTLY UNRECOVERABLE -- since_days=30 and max_messages_per_account=50 are HARDCODED and not request parameters, the original window was 2026-08-07 to 2026-09-06 while a re-run today covers 2026-08-21 to 2026-09-20, so mail dated 2026-08-07 to 2026-08-20 is outside the new window and would stay unreadable even after a successful backfill. (b) THE FAILURE IS SILENT -- the duplicate-path blob write is wrapped in 'except Exception: pass' (ingest.py:85-86), so a failed write still reports state=ingested/duplicate=true and tells the owner it worked; the ONLY trustworthy check is the blob COUNT ON DISK, never the route's response. (c) THE KEY IS DERIVED FROM app.secret_key (app.py:116-120), so if that changed, earlier blobs are undecryptable and read() raising is reported as the same 'not stored yet' 404 -- indistinguishable to the owner from the current condition. (4) SEPARATE DEFECT FOUND WHILE TRIAGING -- BILLS ARE NOT LINKED TO EVIDENCE: evidence_links holds 15 links total and ALL 15 target transaction/documents; ZERO target a bill despite 11 bills in the DB, and only 8 distinct evidence items of 732 are linked to anything. Gmail intake populates link_mail_evidence_to_transactions (meridian/gmail_intake.py:157) and there is NO bill equivalent, so fixing the blob store alone will NOT make bill evidence appear. RECOMMENDED ORDER: widen the intake window FIRST, then re-run Gmail intake, then verify by counting blobs on disk; then make the silent blob-write failure visible; then treat calendar as a new-capability decision (which events become evidence, and under what linking rule) rather than a patch; then the bill-to-evidence linking gap.
